name: The Tourism Recovery Playbook
description: Rebuild the operating spine for the flagship Caribia Resorts beachfront property over five strategic rounds — diagnose the demand reset, re-channel the OTA-versus-direct mix, re-segment by source market, re-mix F&B and capex priorities, and stabilise the labour pipeline. The simulation operationalises the Sigala (2020) reset frame, the Cornell CHR conversion-engine principle, and the Baum et al. (2020) wage-band-inversion finding for hospitality post-pandemic recovery.

Round 1 — Diagnose

Round Decisions

2025 mix — OTA 41% / Direct 17% / GDS 14% / Group 19% / Walk-in 9%. Cornell CHR: each 1pt OTA-to-Direct lifts net ADR by USD 0.45 to 0.55. Sustainable rebalance ceiling: 2 pts/year.
European leisure share has eroded from 28% (2019) to 17% (2025). WTTC 2025: European long-haul forecast to plateau at 75 to 82% of 2019 through 2027. US Premium leisure couples are the modern centre of gravity at 17% of nights and USD 318 ADR.
2025 ratio — F&B 24% / Rooms 64% / Other 12%. Buffet at 71% cover-mix (vs 58% 2019). Selva Verde is on reduced-cover schedule due to line-cook shortage. CFO note: rooms must be renovated by Q3 2027 (USD 1.8M, mandatory). Capex envelope USD 4.8M.
Selected: $1.80M / $4.80M
Housekeeping turnover 47% (paid -3% vs sector). F&B back-of-house turnover 41% (paid -2% vs sector). AHLA 2024: a 12-18% wage adjustment paired with career pathing reduces turnover by 35-45% within 24 months. Replacement cost of a trained line cook is 1.4x annual wage.
